output.answer_markdown:
In EOG's FY2024 10-K, proved reserve estimates are a significant component of the DD&A calculation, so revisions change the rate of future expense. Holding all else constant, an upward revision increases earnings and a downward revision decreases them [7]. DD&A for proved oil and gas properties uses the unit-of-production method [7].

Reserve bases by cost type [7]:
- **Leasehold acquisition costs and the cost to acquire proved properties:** proved developed reserves plus proved undeveloped reserves.
- **Lease and well equipment costs** (development costs and successful exploration drilling costs): proved developed reserves only.

provenance.quote: Holding all other factors constant, if reserves are revised upward or downward, earnings will increase or decrease, respectively.

claims.text: Quantities of estimated proved reserves are a significant component of EOG's DD&A calculation, and revisions in the estimates may alter the rate of future expense; holding other factors constant, upward revisions increase earnings and downward revisions decrease earnings.

provenance.quote: Depreciation, depletion and amortization of the cost of proved oil and gas properties is calculated using the unit-of-production method.

claims.text: DD&A of the cost of proved oil and gas properties is calculated using the unit-of-production method.

provenance.quote: The reserve base used to calculate depreciation, depletion and amortization for leasehold acquisition costs and the cost to acquire proved properties is the sum of proved developed reserves and proved undeveloped reserves.

claims.text: For leasehold acquisition costs and the cost to acquire proved properties, the reserve base is the sum of proved developed reserves and proved undeveloped reserves.

provenance.quote: With respect to lease and well equipment costs, which include development costs and successful exploration drilling costs, the reserve base used includes only proved developed reserves.

claims.text: For lease and well equipment costs, which include development costs and successful exploration drilling costs, the reserve base includes only proved developed reserves.
